label: early original-phase consonant (d/p/s/i/r/k/t) after an earlier q or a
explanation: Sparse unit (about 1% of steps). 91% of activation mass falls in the original phase, peaking at t=2-4, and it never fires at t=0-1 or on the delimiter. It looks like a graded conjunction of history and the current input. Rate rises when q (prev2 lift 8.7x, first_tok 5.0x) or a (4.7x) appeared earlier in the sequence, with weaker contributions from l, 1 and n. Rate also rises when the current input is d/p/s/i/r/k/t (2.6-4.3x). The strongest activations are on the 3rd-5th original tokens of sequences that begin with runs of q or a, e.g. a q q q [p]. It rarely fires on q/a inputs themselves, on late original positions (t>=6), or in the copy phase (about 9% of mass, mostly recall_idx 2-3). The predicate catches about 57% of mass but has low precision (~0.22), because many q/a-then-consonant steps stay silent. The contributions look additive and distributed rather than a crisp rule.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the input two steps back (most: q, a, l, 1, n, c; least: e, r, h, -) and the current input token, by step (t=9: r, d, k, h; t=11: r, d, h, k; t=10: r, d, h, k); timing cues that raise it most: L=4 & t=3, t=3, L=5 & t=4.
